name: Send quote follow-up emails on a 3-7-14 day schedule with Gmail and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Quote follow-ups that never slip — and stop the moment they should

### How it works
You track outgoing quotes in one Google Sheet. Once a day, this workflow reads every open quote, works out how many days have passed since you sent it, and emails the right follow-up at day 3, day 7 and day 14 — each with its own tone (friendly nudge → value reminder → polite close-out). The moment you mark a quote `won` or `lost` in the sheet, follow-ups stop instantly. Every send is written back to the sheet, so a quote can never get the same follow-up twice, even if you re-run the workflow manually.

No AI key needed — the three templates are plain text with placeholders, so this runs 100% free.

### Setup
1. Connect **Gmail** and **Google Sheets** (one-click Google sign-in on n8n Cloud).
2. Make a sheet with headers: `quote_id, customer_name, customer_email, quote_amount, sent_date, status, followup_1, followup_2, followup_3` — set `status` to `open` and `sent_date` as YYYY-MM-DD.
3. Select your sheet in both Sheets nodes, put your business details in **⚙️ Your settings**, and edit the three templates to sound like you.
4. Activate. It checks once a day at 9am.

### Customization tips
Change the day offsets, subjects and body text in ⚙️ Your settings. Add a fourth touch by copying a template block.

## 1. Read the quote ledger
Runs daily at 9am. Pulls every row from your quotes sheet — the sheet stays the single source of truth that you and the workflow both edit.

## 2. Decide what is due
Keeps only quotes with status `open`, computes days since `sent_date`, and picks which follow-up (if any) is due today — skipping any step already marked as sent. This double guard (status + sent-flags) is what makes re-runs safe: no customer ever gets a duplicate.

## 3. Send + write back
Fills the right template with the customer's name, amount and your details, sends it from your Gmail, then immediately stamps the sheet (`followup_N = date`). Write-back happens right after each send, so even a crash mid-run cannot cause a double email tomorrow.
